thread.title: Tech Stock Funds Top List Of Best ETFs Over The Past Decade | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Tech Stock Funds Top List Of Best ETFs Over The Past Decade | Investor's Business Daily
text:
An exchange traded fund can have a great year now and then. But the true test is if it can perform well enough to produce solid gains over the long haul. So which are the best ETFs?
X We ran a screen for the top-performing non-leveraged U.S. ETFs based on their average annual returns over the past 10 years. Funds had to meet criteria including a minimum amount of assets, as well as average daily volume of at least 50,000 shares. Keep in mind that the current bull market is now well into its ninth year, which sets the bar high for outperformance.
Sector Funds Among The Best ETFs So here's what we found. Many tech-focused ETFs, including biotech, internet and semiconductor, were among the best ETFs. In terms of categories, then, sector funds were the leaders, with a few big-cap growth funds also among the biggest gainers.
Top 10 performers include First Trust Dow Jones Internet ( FDN ) with a 10-year annualized return of 20.8%. The 12-year-old fund has amassed $9.5 billion in assets. The hot FANG stocks — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ) — made up nearly a third, or 33%, of the 41-stock portfolio.

Please contact customer service CLOSE IShares PHLX Semiconductor ( SOXX ), made the list with a 10-year annualized return of 16.9%. The $1.6 billion fund, which tracks the PHLX SOX Semiconductor Index, owns 30 chip stocks including Broadcom ( AVGO ), Qualcomm ( QCOM ), Intel ( INTC ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ). The index has trended higher since late 2000, driven by widespread use of semiconductors in everything from smartphones to cars.
Invesco QQQ Trust ( QQQ ), a widely used barometer for big-cap tech stocks, also made a strong showing with a 16.7% average annual return. The $71.3 billion fund, which tracks the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100, is topped by Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon, Microsoft ( MSFT ), Alphabet and Facebook.
Outpacing The Market By comparison, SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) produced a 10-year average annual return of 11%, according to Morningstar Direct. SPY tracks the broader market.
Now, let's take a look at the best ETFs including leveraged funds, based on 10-year average annual returns. Leveraged funds tend to undergo wider swings, since they usually aim for double or triple the daily return (or inverse) of an index. So while they can produce big gains quickly, investors can also suffer big losses in a short time. They also tend to carry higher expense ratios than their non-leveraged counterparts.
ProShares Ultra QQQ ( QLD ) came out on top with a 28.6% annualized return over the past 10 years. The $2.1 billion fund shoots for twice the daily performance of the Nasdaq 100 index. It carries a 0.95% expense ratio. QQQ charges 0.20%.
ProShares Ultra Dow 30 ( DDM ), with $437 million in assets, has produced a 10-year average return of 18.4%. This leveraged play targets twice the daily performance of the Dow Jones industrial average. It charges 0.95%. The non-leveraged SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) costs 0.17%.
